findings.mechanism: Each parsed Tree is a reference cycle (Node.parent<->children, Node.tree<->Tree.root/by_path), so it is freed only by the cyclic GC, not refcounting. tuning.install() (called in OutlineService.__init__) raises the gen0 threshold to 40000, so garbage trees pile up for several thousand conversions before each collection, giving a sawtooth that looks like a rising memory graph.
findings.cause: gc.set_threshold(40_000, 20, 20) delays collection of cyclic Node/Tree garbage; nothing is retained by any long-lived holder (OutlineService keeps only an int counter, OutlineResult holds only strings/ints).
findings.evidence: Ran load.run(2000) six times on one service and sampled gc.get_objects(): 20.5k -> 28.7k -> 35k -> 43k -> 51k live objects, then dropped to 16.8k when the gen0 threshold was reached; gc.collect() reclaimed 5552 objects and left ~11.3k (baseline). With default thresholds the count stayed flat at ~13-15k. Peak RSS plateaued at ~22-23MB vs ~15MB with default thresholds, with no unbounded growth.
findings.discriminator: Object count and RSS drop/plateau once the collector runs (gc.collect() frees the trees); with default GC thresholds there is no growth. The memory is bounded, reclaimable garbage, not retained. Possible mitigation (not applied): lower the threshold or break cycles (weakref parent/tree).
